name: IE
title: Ireland Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in Irish politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with Fine Gael, Fianna Fáil, Sinn Féin, the Greens, Labour and the Social Democrats, plus your framing bias.
keywords: Irish political quiz, Ireland compass test, Sinn Féin Fine Gael Fianna Fáil, Ireland election 2026, political alignment test Ireland, Irish party quiz

fg.name: Fine Gael
fg.desc: Your answers most closely align with Fine Gael. You favour a pro-business environment, low corporate taxes, fiscal restraint, and socially progressive values.

ff.name: Fianna Fáil
ff.desc: Your answers most closely align with Fianna Fáil. You represent a centrist republican position that balances support for business with state-backed housing initiatives.

sf.name: Sinn Féin
sf.desc: Your answers most closely align with Sinn Féin. You strongly advocate for Irish reunification, massive state builds in housing, wealth taxes, and protecting Irish neutrality.

grn.name: Green Party
grn.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Green Party. You prioritise aggressive carbon reduction, cycling infrastructure, and sustainable economic reform.

lab.name: Labour Party
lab.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Labour Party. You support workers' rights, enhanced public services, and progressive social taxation.

sd.name: Social Democrats
sd.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Social Democrats. You want universal healthcare (Sláintecare), strict political accountability, and massive public housing investment.

ind.name: Independent
ind.desc: Your answers do not strongly align with a single party. You hold pragmatic, local, or mixed views typical of Ireland's large independent voting base.

bank.q: The state should build council and public housing on a massive scale to end the crisis.
bank.ctx: 'Council housing' is government-owned rental housing. This supports building it on a massive scale to end a severe housing crisis of soaring rents and homelessness. The stake is how directly the state should provide housing.

bank.q: The housing fix is backing private developers and cutting red tape, not more state building.
bank.ctx: This argues the fix is backing private developers and cutting the planning red tape that slows building, not more state construction. The stake is whether government or the market should lead on housing.

bank.q: A long-term rent freeze should be imposed to protect tenants.
bank.ctx: A 'rent freeze' legally stops rents rising. This supports a long-term one to protect tenants amid unaffordable rents in Dublin and other cities. The stake is protecting tenants versus housing supply.

bank.q: Rent freezes drive landlords out and worsen the shortage for everyone.
bank.ctx: This argues rent freezes drive landlords out of the market and worsen the shortage for everyone, as many small landlords sell up. The stake is whether freezing rents helps or backfires on renters.

bank.q: Ireland is taking in too many asylum seekers and immigration should be cut.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland is taking in too many asylum seekers — numbers rose sharply — and that immigration should be cut, a newer issue in Irish politics that has sparked protests. The stake is whether Ireland's capacity is being overrun.

bank.q: Ireland, a nation of emigrants, has a duty to welcome people fleeing hardship.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland, historically a nation of emigrants who fled famine and poverty, has a special duty to welcome people fleeing hardship. The stake is Ireland's own history shaping how it treats migrants.

bank.q: Communities should have a real say before asylum centres are placed in their area.
bank.ctx: This argues local communities should have a real say before asylum-seeker centres are opened in their area, after protests over centres imposed without consultation. The stake is local voice versus central decisions on housing migrants.

bank.q: Local vetoes over asylum housing just give cover to intimidation and racism.
bank.ctx: This argues letting communities veto asylum housing gives cover to intimidation and racism, some of it linked to arson attacks on planned centres. The stake is local consent versus protecting asylum seekers.

bank.q: There should be a referendum on a united Ireland within the next decade.
bank.ctx: A 'united Ireland' would join the Republic with Northern Ireland (part of the UK). This wants a referendum — a 'border poll' — within a decade, a prospect revived by Brexit and Sinn Féin's rise. The stake is Irish reunification.

bank.q: A border poll now would be divisive and destabilising, and should not be rushed.
bank.ctx: This argues a border poll now would be divisive and destabilising — risking a return to sectarian tension — and should not be rushed. The stake is the timing and wisdom of a unity vote.

bank.q: Ireland should hold firmly to its military neutrality and stay out of NATO.
bank.ctx: Ireland is militarily neutral and not in NATO. This supports holding firmly to that neutrality, a long-standing part of Irish identity. The stake is staying out of military alliances.

bank.q: In a dangerous world Ireland can no longer freeload on others’ defence and should deepen western alliances.
bank.ctx: This argues that in a more dangerous world, neutrality means freeloading on others' defence, and Ireland should deepen ties with Western allies. The stake is neutrality versus shared security.

bank.q: Ireland should move to a single-tier public health system and end private care in public hospitals.
bank.ctx: Ireland has a mixed public-private health system with long public waiting lists. This supports moving to a single-tier public system (the 'Sláintecare' plan) and ending private care in public hospitals. The stake is ending a two-tier system.

bank.q: Private healthcare relieves pressure on the public system, and abolishing it would make waits worse.
bank.ctx: This argues private healthcare relieves pressure on the public system, and abolishing it would make waits worse. The stake is whether private care helps or entrenches inequality.

bank.q: The wealthiest and highest earners should pay significantly more tax.
bank.ctx: This supports significantly higher taxes on the wealthiest and highest earners to fund services and housing. The stake is whether the top should pay more.

bank.q: Higher taxes on the successful just drive investment and talent out of Ireland.
bank.ctx: This argues higher taxes on the successful drive investment and talent out of Ireland. The stake is whether taxing the top raises revenue or repels it.

bank.q: Ireland’s low corporate tax rate is vital and must be protected.
bank.ctx: Ireland's low 12.5% corporate tax rate lured multinationals like Apple and Google, whose taxes and jobs underpin the economy. This argues it is vital and must be protected. The stake is defending a cornerstone of Ireland's economic model.

bank.q: Ireland’s low corporate tax is a race to the bottom that starves public services.
bank.ctx: This argues the low corporate tax is a 'race to the bottom' that starves other countries and public services of revenue, and leaves Ireland dangerously reliant on a few US firms. The stake is whether the model is smart or unsustainable.

bank.q: Ireland must cut emissions faster, including from its large farming sector.
bank.ctx: This supports cutting emissions faster, including from Ireland's large cattle and dairy farming sector, its biggest emissions source. The stake is climate action versus the farming economy.

bank.q: Climate rules that punish Irish farmers threaten rural life for tiny global gain.
bank.ctx: This argues climate rules that hit Irish farmers threaten rural life and communities for tiny global benefit. The stake is protecting farming versus climate goals.

bank.q: Irish farmers are unfairly targeted by climate policy and deserve more protection.
bank.ctx: This argues Irish farmers are unfairly targeted by climate and EU rules and deserve far more protection. The stake is whether farmers are being scapegoated.

bank.q: Farming must meet the same environmental standards as everyone else, not be exempted.
bank.ctx: This argues farming must meet the same environmental standards as everyone else, not be exempted. The stake is whether agriculture deserves special treatment.

bank.q: Legalising abortion in 2018 was the right decision for Ireland.
bank.ctx: In a landmark 2018 referendum, Ireland — once deeply Catholic — voted two-to-one to legalise abortion, repealing its constitutional ban. This defends that as the right decision. The stake is Ireland's liberal transformation.

bank.q: Legalising abortion was a moral wrong, and Ireland went too far.
bank.ctx: This argues legalising abortion was a moral wrong and that Ireland went too far. The stake is the moral status of the unborn.

bank.q: The Irish language should be actively promoted and given more support.
bank.ctx: This supports actively promoting and funding the Irish (Gaelic) language, a national symbol spoken fluently by a minority. The stake is reviving a heritage language.

bank.q: Compulsory Irish and heavy spending on the language are a waste that few actually use.
bank.ctx: This argues compulsory Irish in schools and heavy spending on the language are wasteful since few people use it daily. The stake is language revival versus practical value.

bank.q: The Catholic Church should have no role in running schools and hospitals.
bank.ctx: The Catholic Church still runs most Irish primary schools and many hospitals, a legacy now widely questioned after abuse scandals. This argues it should have no such role. The stake is removing the Church from public services.

bank.q: The Church’s role in Irish education and care is part of the country’s heritage and does good.
bank.ctx: This argues the Church's role in Irish education and care is part of the country's heritage and does genuine good. The stake is tradition and service versus secular control.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with Irish values.
bank.ctx: This argues Islam clashes with Irish values. Critics call it prejudice against a small but growing community. The stake is whether the concern is legitimate or bigoted.

bank.q: Muslim Irish people are full members of society, and their faith deserves equal respect.
bank.ctx: This holds that Muslim Irish people are full members of society whose faith deserves equal respect. The stake is religious equality versus singling out one faith.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are innately more intelligent or capable than others. It was the ideological engine of Nazism and the Holocaust, and of systems like slavery and apartheid. Modern genetics finds more variation within any racial group than between them, and the idea has no scientific standing.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This states the principle of fundamental human equality: that no race is innately superior in intelligence or ability, and that racial hierarchies are discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history behind slavery and apartheid. It is the moral baseline of modern anti-discrimination law.

bank.q: Ireland needs more Gardí on the streets and tougher sentences for violent crime.
bank.ctx: The Gardí are Ireland's police. This argues Ireland needs more of them on the streets and tougher sentences for violent crime, after high-profile incidents. The stake is whether more policing and punishment improve safety.

bank.q: More police and longer sentences have never cut crime; prevention and services do.
bank.ctx: This argues more police and longer sentences have never cut crime, and that prevention and social services do. The stake is what actually reduces crime.

bank.q: Trans people should be able to change their legal gender by self-identification.
bank.ctx: This supports transgender rights: letting people have the law recognise the gender they identify as and access gender-affirming care. 'Self-identification' laws, used in countries like Ireland and Argentina, allow a legal gender change without medical gatekeeping. The stake is whether gender is defined by identity or by biology.

bank.q: Biological sex is a reality the law should not let a declaration override.
bank.ctx: This is the 'gender-critical' view: that biological sex is a fixed, binary reality no declaration or surgery can change, and that the law should rest on it — in single-sex spaces, sport, and official data. Associated with feminists like J.K. Rowling, it clashes head-on with the identity-based view.

bank.q: Workers need stronger unions and rights, and a higher living wage.
bank.ctx: This supports stronger unions and worker rights and a higher 'living wage' above the legal minimum. The stake is the balance of power between workers and employers.

bank.q: Union power and higher mandated wages just cost jobs and hurt small businesses.
bank.ctx: This argues union power and higher mandated wages cost jobs and hurt small businesses. The stake is protecting workers versus business costs.

bank.q: Ireland’s social welfare payments should be raised to protect people from poverty.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland's welfare payments should be raised to protect people from poverty amid the high cost of living. The stake is the adequacy of the safety net.

bank.q: Raising welfare too far just weakens the incentive to work.
bank.ctx: This argues raising welfare too far weakens the incentive to work. The stake is balancing support against work incentives.

bank.q: Ireland over-regulates business; companies need less red tape and lower costs.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland over-regulates business and companies need less red tape and lower costs. The stake is whether deregulation would help the economy.

bank.q: Cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment.
bank.ctx: This argues cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment. The stake is whether rules protect people or burden business.

bank.q: Drug use should be decriminalised and treated as a health issue.
bank.ctx: This supports decriminalising drug use and treating it as a health issue, following models like Portugal's. The stake is whether prohibition or a health approach works better.

bank.q: Going soft on drugs fuels addiction and disorder, and it should be resisted.
bank.ctx: This argues softening drug laws fuels addiction and disorder and should be resisted. The stake is whether easing drug laws helps or hurts.

bank.q: Ireland should legalise assisted dying for the terminally ill.
bank.ctx: This supports legalising assisted dying (medical help to die) for the terminally ill, a live issue Ireland has been examining. The stake is control over one's own death.

bank.q: Assisted dying puts pressure on the vulnerable and crosses a line society should not cross.
bank.ctx: This argues assisted dying pressures the vulnerable and crosses a line society shouldn't cross. The stake is whether the safeguards protect the vulnerable.

bank.q: Ireland’s place is at the heart of a strong European Union.
bank.ctx: This sees Ireland's future at the heart of a strong European Union — broadly popular in a country that has benefited hugely from EU membership. The stake is deepening Ireland's EU commitment.

bank.q: Brussels has too much power over Ireland, and Irish sovereignty should come first.
bank.ctx: This argues Brussels has too much power over Ireland and that Irish sovereignty should come first. The stake is national control versus EU integration.

bank.q: Vulture funds and big investors should be blocked from buying up Irish homes.
bank.ctx: 'Vulture funds' are large international investors that bought up Irish property and mortgages in bulk after the 2008 crash. This supports blocking them from buying up homes. The stake is curbing investor dominance of housing.

bank.q: Investment funds add much-needed housing supply, and blocking them would backfire.
bank.ctx: This argues investment funds add much-needed housing supply, and blocking them would backfire by cutting building. The stake is whether such investors help or harm the housing market.

bank.q: Ireland’s system of many referendums on big questions is a strength worth keeping.
bank.ctx: Ireland amends its constitution only by referendum and holds many. This argues that system — which delivered marriage equality and abortion reform — is a strength worth keeping. The stake is the value of frequent direct votes.

bank.q: Constant referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and cause needless division.
bank.ctx: This argues constant referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and cause needless division, as recent failed votes suggested. The stake is whether Ireland over-uses referendums.

bank.q: Ireland should take a strong public stance for Palestinian rights, even at diplomatic cost.
bank.ctx: This supports Ireland taking a strong public stand for Palestinian rights — as it did by recognising a Palestinian state — even at a diplomatic cost. The stake is a values-driven foreign policy versus diplomatic caution.

bank.q: Ireland should stay balanced on the Middle East rather than taking sides.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland should stay balanced on the Middle East rather than taking sides. The stake is moral stance versus neutrality in foreign affairs.

bank.q: Protecting nature should take priority over new roads, data centres, and development.
bank.ctx: 'Data centres' are power-hungry computer facilities that now consume a large and rising share of Ireland's electricity. This puts protecting nature ahead of new roads, data centres, and development. The stake is conservation versus development and tech investment.

bank.q: Endless environmental objections are strangling the housing and infrastructure Ireland needs.
bank.ctx: This argues endless environmental objections block the housing and infrastructure Ireland desperately needs. The stake is whether green rules protect nature or block progress.

bank.q: The government should intervene directly to cap energy and rent costs.
bank.ctx: This supports the government intervening directly to cap energy and rent costs amid the cost-of-living crisis. The stake is how far the state should intervene in prices.

bank.q: Price caps cause shortages and drive suppliers out; they don’t fix the cost of living.
bank.ctx: This argues price caps cause shortages and drive suppliers out without fixing the real problem. The stake is whether intervention helps or worsens the cost of living.

bank.q: Immigrants should adapt to Irish culture and values, not the other way around.
bank.ctx: This argues immigrants should adapt to Irish culture and values rather than the country adapting to them. The stake is how much cultural conformity to expect of newcomers.

bank.q: A living culture is always a blend; demanding assimilation impoverishes Ireland.
bank.ctx: This argues a living culture is always a blend, so demanding assimilation impoverishes Ireland. The stake is integration versus multiculturalism.

bank.q: Ireland should increase defence spending and take its own security more seriously.
bank.ctx: This supports higher defence spending and Ireland taking its own security more seriously, given its tiny military and exposure. The stake is whether neutral Ireland should invest more in defence.

bank.q: Money for the military is money that should go to housing and health instead.
bank.ctx: This argues money for the military would be better spent on housing and health. The stake is priorities between defence and social needs.

bank.q: RTÉ and public broadcasting are worth funding and must stay independent.
bank.ctx: RTÉ is Ireland's public broadcaster, whose reputation was dented by a 2023 payments scandal. This argues it is still worth funding and must stay independent. The stake is the value and independence of public media.

bank.q: RTÉ is wasteful and out of touch, and its licence fee should be scrapped.
bank.ctx: This argues RTÉ is wasteful and out of touch and its licence fee should be scrapped. The stake is whether public broadcasting deserves its funding.

bank.q: The unemployed are treated with too much suspicion; the safety net should be stronger.
bank.ctx: This argues the unemployed are treated with too much suspicion and the safety net should be stronger. The stake is how generous and accessible welfare should be.

bank.q: Welfare too easily becomes a trap, and stricter conditions protect taxpayers who fund it.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare can trap people, and stricter conditions protect the taxpayers who fund it. The stake is whether conditions on aid help or punish recipients.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions carry the wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative philosophy of tradition, associated with Edmund Burke: that long-standing customs and institutions hold the accumulated, hard-won wisdom of generations, so change should be gradual and cautious rather than sweeping away what works for untested ideas.

bank.q: Worshipping tradition just lets the dead govern the living and blocks necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply, in the spirit of Thomas Paine's line that 'the dead should not govern the living': that treating tradition as sacred just lets the prejudices of the past block overdue reform — as appeals to tradition once defended slavery and denying women the vote.

bank.q: A good society depends more on personal responsibility than on government support.
bank.ctx: This reflects a core right-leaning value: that a healthy society depends mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own choices and lives, and that leaning too heavily on government breeds dependence and saps initiative.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems the system creates is how the comfortable excuse others’ suffering.
bank.ctx: This reflects a core left-leaning value: that many hardships — poverty, poor health, joblessness — stem from unfair systems and circumstances beyond personal control, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable ignore problems they benefit from or could help fix.

heroTitle:
Where do you stand in
Irish politics?
heroSub: 70 statements on the issues defining Ireland right now: housing, immigration, a united Ireland, neutrality, and health. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, revealing both your party alignment and your framing bias.
